name: Hayley Williams
description:
'''Hayley Nichole Williams''' (born December 27, 1988) is an American singer and songwriter. She is the lead vocalist and a founding member of the rock band [[Paramore]] and has released several solo albums. In 2023, ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' ranked her as the 13th greatest rock lead singer of all time; that same year, ''[[Alternative Press (magazine)|Alternative Press]]'' readers voted her as the second greatest [[pop-punk]] vocalist of all time.

Born and raised in [[Meridian, Mississippi]], Williams and her mother moved to [[Franklin, Tennessee]], following her parents' divorce, there forming Paramore with [[Josh Farro]], [[Zac Farro]], and [[Jeremy Davis]]. Since, the band has released six studio albums: ''[[All We Know Is Falling]]'' (2005), ''[[Riot!]]'' (2007), ''[[Brand New Eyes]]'' (2009), ''[[Paramore (album)|Paramore]]'' (2013), ''[[After Laughter]]'' (2017), and ''[[This Is Why]]'' (2023). The group has continuously changed [[Paramore#Band members|its lineup]] (currently consisting of Williams, Zac Farro, and [[Taylor York]]), with Williams being the only member to appear on all six albums. Along with York, Williams won the 2015 [[Grammy Award for Best Rock Song]] for Paramore's song "[[Ain't It Fun (Paramore song)|Ain't It Fun]]".

Williams' work outside Paramore includes the song "Teenagers" for the soundtrack of the film ''[[Jennifer's Body]]'' (2009) and collaborations with [[New Found Glory]], [[Zedd]], [[American Football (band)|American Football]], [[Moses Sumney]], [[Turnstile (band)|Turnstile]], and [[David Byrne]]. In 2010, she was featured on the single "[[Airplanes (song)|Airplanes]]" by [[B.o.B]], which peaked at No. 2 on the U.S. [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]]. The song's sequel, "[[Airplanes (song)#"Airplanes, Part II"|Airplanes, Part II]]", still featuring Williams and adding a guest verse by [[Eminem]], gained a nomination for the [[Grammy Award for Best Pop Collaboration with Vocals]]. In 2023, she featured on "[[Castles Crumbling]]", a song on [[Taylor Swift]]'s re-recorded album ''[[Speak Now (Taylor's Version)]]''.

As a solo artist, Williams released the [[extended plays]] ''[[Petals for Armor I]]'' and ''[[Petals for Armor II]]'' (both 2020), the subsequent full-length album ''[[Petals for Armor]]'' (2020), and her second album ''[[Flowers for Vases / Descansos]]'' (2021). In 2025, she released her third album ''[[Ego Death at a Bachelorette Party]]'' under her own [[Independent record label|independent label]] named Post Atlantic; the album earned her three [[Grammy Award]] nominations. In 2026, she began the musical project Power Snatch with producer [[Canon Blue|Daniel James]]. Her other ventures include the online series ''Kiss-Off'' (2015) and the [[hair dye]] company Good Dye Young.
